questions.question: Please agree the English wordplay. Russian “khimichit” can mean doing chemistry or fiddling results, creating a joke across mathematics, physics and chemistry. “Cook up a result” preserves the suggestion of fabrication, but the chemistry reference is less explicit.

localizations.source: Please agree the English wordplay. Russian “khimichit” can mean doing chemistry or fiddling results, creating a joke across mathematics, physics and chemistry. “Cook up a result” preserves the suggestion of fabrication, but the chemistry reference is less explicit.
localizations.ru: В исходнике «химичить» означает и заниматься химией, и жульничать или подгонять результат; на столкновении математики, физики и химии построена развязка. В EN предложено “Mathematics isn’t physics, where you can cook up a result…”, сохраняющее намёк на фабрикацию, но химическое значение менее явное. Согласовать английскую игру слов перед публикацией.

questions.resolution: “Cook up a result in the lab” carries the suggestion of fabrication and the laboratory setting into the English punchline.
